Hi Rajiv / Acme infra team —

Following up from last week's call: attached is the first pass of reference diagrams and a proposed cutover checklist for the private VPC deployment. The goal of this thread is to lock down the control plane/data plane boundaries and call out any compliance or connectivity constraints before we freeze the runbook.

Attachments: [Attachment: reference-diagram-v1.png (image/png)], [Attachment: cutover-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Key asks:
- Can you confirm whether your environment will allow a managed VPC endpoint for the control plane (we recommend a private endpoint + NAT egress for updates/audit logs)?
- Any constraints on outbound TLS inspection or proxying that would affect KV cache sync or telemetry?
- Preferred 2-hour window in the week of Dec 20 for the cutover dry-run?

Proposed next steps: internal review + we send an updated diagram with control-plane egress detail by EOD tomorrow. If there are compliance items (log forwarding, retention) we can include them in the cutover checklist.

Thanks —

Thanks Rajiv — appreciate the detail. Quick answers and an updated artifact attached.

1) Audit logs / telemetry:
- By default audit logs are pushed to a customer-controlled S3/GCS bucket (we will not retain telemetry in Redwood-managed storage unless explicitly configured).
- The control plane will send summarized usage/health metrics to Redwood for SLA telemetry only if you opt in; this can be toggled in the private control plane config.

2) Proxy/egress behavior:
- The control-plane agent supports authenticating forward proxies (we currently support basic auth and mTLS with a client cert).
- For KV cache synchronization and model pulls, we recommend allowing egress to the following FQDNs (or route via your proxy): control.redwood-inference.com, updates.redwood-inference.com.

3) Network specifics (high level):
- Control plane: runs in your VPC (private subnet) with a single outbound path through your central NAT/proxy. Ports 443 outbound required, port 22 only for optional support tunnel (disabled by default).
- Data plane: model inference nodes run in customer-managed compute (on-prem / private cloud) or dedicated pools; traffic between app and data plane stays inside your network unless you route tokens to Redwood-hosted variants (opt-in).

Attached: [Attachment: reference-diagram-v2.png (image/png)] — this callout highlights the egress path to your S3 for audit logs.

Action items:
- Kimberly: confirm dry-run slot (we have Dec 21 10:00–12:00 PST tentatively).
- Rajiv: confirm proxy auth method and whether you’ll allow the support tunnel for the dry-run (optional).

Will update the cutover checklist after we get those answers.

Cheers,

Kimberly / team —

Couple of technical clarifications to surface before we finalize the diagram:
- We should call out the expected prefix list and recommend using AWS VPC endpoints for S3 access to avoid NAT egress where possible. I annotated port/endpoint notes on v2 (see attached reference-diagram-v2).
- For the optional support tunnel: it will originate from a support pod inside the private control plane and be initiated only during a support session; we use a short-lived mTLS cert tied to the session — no persistent inbound holes required.
- If Acme requires TLS inspection that terminates TLS at the proxy, we need to confirm whether client certificate verification still functions; if not, we'll plan for mutual TLS to terminate inside your boundary and use header-based auth to the proxy.
